label: GO late in episode (trial >~80), scaled by previous trial; largest after a2 -> S1 rare unrewarded
terms: (phase == GO) * 1/(1+np.exp(-(ep_trial-85)/4)) * last_is("a2 S1 u") ;; (phase == GO) * 1/(1+np.exp(-(ep_trial-85)/4)) * last_is("a2 S2 u") ;; (phase == GO) * 1/(1+np.exp(-(ep_trial-85)/4)) * last_is("a1 S1 u") ;; (phase == GO) * 1/(1+np.exp(-(ep_trial-85)/4)) * last_is("a2 S1 r") ;; (phase == GO) * 1/(1+np.exp(-(ep_trial-85)/4)) * (prev_reward == 1) ;; (phase == GO) * 1/(1+np.exp(-(ep_trial-85)/4)) * (prev_reward == 0) * (prev_action == -1) ;; (phase == GO) * 1/(1+np.exp(-(ep_trial-85)/4)) * np.clip(-belief_lo,-4,4)
explanation: Fires only at GO, and only late in the episode (gain is roughly a sigmoid of ep_trial centred at about 85). Within that late GO window the size is set by the previous trial: biggest after a2 -> S1 rare unrewarded (weight about +2.3 on the late gate), medium after a2 -> S1 rare rewarded (+0.5), a2 -> S2 common unrewarded (+0.4) and a1 -> S1 common unrewarded (+0.26). Any rewarded previous trial suppresses it (-0.4). On the window's first trial, where the previous choice is unknown, an unrewarded previous outcome raises it (+0.7). Graded ideal-observer belief that S2 is good adds very little (dev 0.781 -> 0.796). D1 and D2 are always 0. Observed-only, with no value or policy terms: dev R^2 beyond timing 0.796, test 0.786. That is far above the profile's additive ceiling 'all' = 0.17, because the late-episode x previous-trial interaction is multiplicative. Leaving out the model's value or policy costs essentially nothing. Choices and states on this trial (future) were not needed.

issues: The core claims hold up. The feature is exactly 0 at D1 and D2. At GO the timing baseline goes 0 up to decile 6, then 0.019 at decile 7, 0.155 at decile 8 and 0.41 at decile 9. Sweeping the sigmoid's centre and width (80-90, 2-6) puts the best fit at about 85-88 with width about 4, giving test 0.769-0.772 without the belief term. In the residual table, a2 S1 u is clearly the largest at GO (+0.346 vs at most +0.049 for the next).

The '+0.5 after a2->S1 rare rewarded' claim misleads. That term stacks on the general rewarded term (-0.41 to -0.45), so the net effect relative to unrewarded a1->S2 is about +0.07 to +0.09. It is only about +0.5 relative to other rewarded trials. The raw residual agrees: a2 S1 r is -0.003, against about -0.056 for the other rewarded patterns.

'Graded belief adds very little' is only true for an additive belief term. Making belief_lo multiply the window-first-trial term and the a2 S1 u term lifts dev from 0.785 to 0.838 and test from 0.774 to 0.824, on the same sigmoid gate (centre 87). The first-trial term (prev_action == -1, unrewarded) has weight 0.44 per unit of -belief_lo. So the flat '+0.7 on the window's first trial' is really strongly belief-dependent: it is large when the observer believes S2 is good.

Misses on the original terms show a systematic class: window-first trials (rel -3) where the actual value is about 3.0 but the prediction is about 1.0 (t91, t93, t95, t96 windows). These are partly fixed by the belief interaction.

Remaining errors follow the agent's upcoming choice. The feature reaches about 2.2 when the agent picks a2 after a1 S1 c u, where about 0.4 is predicted, and is 0 when it picks a1 after a2 S2 u, where about 0.77 is predicted. Conditioning on the future action as well (8 terms) only reaches test 0.794-0.808, below the 0.824 of the observed belief-interaction version. So there is no cheap future-variable fix, and the gap left from not using the model's own outputs is small.
Overall the gap is moderate (+0.04 test R^2), not a large unexplained class. The original 0.786 test score is reproduced.
